title: Unplaceable-reference: one rule for references a reader elsewhere cannot resolve
summary: This change adds a single new writing rule, `unplaceable-reference`, that replaces six older reference rules (bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, undefined-name-at-start). The new rule scans each paragraph for four kinds of candidate — numbers, phrases, times and names — and reports the ones the paragraph itself does not place (no link, no bracketed description, no repository, no absolute date, no definition). It also introduces an `Evidence` axis in the lint core: a finding backed only by statistical evidence (a guessed name, a quoted term, a developer-tool name) always resolves to a warning that advises, never to an error that blocks a reply, in every context. The bulk of the diff is the new candidate extractor, its fixture corpus, and end-to-end tests through the stop hook, commit-message check and prompt hook.

lanes.label: Lint surfaces
lanes.subtitle: where text enters the linter
lanes.summary: The three entry points that hand text to the writing lint: the stop hook on an assistant reply, the commit-message check, and the prompt hook reminder.

lanes.label: Writing lint
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing
lanes.summary: The rule pipeline that turns a document into findings: per-sentence rules, undefined names, the new unplaceable-reference rule, and context resolution.

lanes.label: Reference analysis
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs
lanes.summary: The new candidate extractor and placement logic: four candidate kinds, quote masking, and the checks that decide whether a paragraph places a candidate.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf-lint-core
lanes.summary: Shared types and the level/remediation matrix, now keyed on evidence as well as class, group, context and exception.

lanes.label: Fixtures and tests
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/hook.rs
nodes.summary: Reads the assistant's last message from stdin and refuses the turn (exit 2) when a blocking finding is present. A new test pins that a reply whose only finding is a weak-evidence name is not refused.

nodes.label: Commit-message check
nodes.subtitle: osf lint writing --context commit
nodes.summary: Lints a commit message file. The new rule runs here in commit context, where a relative time such as `yesterday` is a finding, unlike in a transcript.

nodes.label: Prompt hook
nodes.subtitle: osf hook prompt
nodes.summary: Prints the reminder shown on every prompt. A new test asserts it never names one of the six retired rule ids.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: The writing pipeline. It now calls `rules::unplaceable_reference` after `undefined_names`, and `apply_context` resolves the new rule with the finding's own evidence while older rules keep deterministic evidence until retired.

nodes.label: unplaceable_reference
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/rules.rs
nodes.summary: The new rule. It gathers candidates per paragraph, keeps the first use of each name, picks one paragraph to report a repeated name from, and emits a finding for every candidate the paragraph does not place.

nodes.label: Placement checks
nodes.subtitle: is_placed, number_is_placed, name_is_placed, tool_is_placed
nodes.summary: Decides whether a paragraph places a candidate: links, bracketed or colon descriptions, appositives, repository slugs, file names, absolute dates, known names, definers and mention markers.

nodes.label: Rule metadata
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/meta.rs
nodes.summary: Adds the `unplaceable-reference` doc entry and threads `Evidence` through `RuleMeta::resolve`. Several example strings were reworded to avoid the new rule firing on the docs themselves.

nodes.label: candidates()
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs
nodes.summary: Extracts number, phrase, time and name candidates from one paragraph, masking quoted and backticked spans first so their contents are never matched as references.

nodes.label: Number candidates
nodes.subtitle: hash refs, word-and-number, word-and-bracket
nodes.summary: Finds `#12`, `repo#125`, `issue 31`, `mechanism (b)` and similar, then excludes versions, years, ranges, counts of nouns, measures, coordinates, citations and known names followed by a number.

nodes.label: Name candidates
nodes.subtitle: capitalised runs, quoted terms, dev tools
nodes.summary: Finds capitalised runs with weak evidence, lowercase double-quoted terms, and developer-tool names in backticks or bare, with `moon` treated as ambiguous unless next to `task runner`.

nodes.label: Quote masking
nodes.subtitle: quoted_spans, mask_quotes
nodes.summary: Pairs double, single, curly and backtick spans, rejecting apostrophes and over-long single-quoted spans, so a quoted mention is never read as a use.

nodes.label: Known names
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing/names.rs
nodes.summary: Adds `is_generic_word` and new built-in names (React, Vite, Tauri, Material, Fluent, RFC, Sonnet, Opus, Haiku) so a version after them is not a candidate.

nodes.label: resolve()
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf-lint-core/src/meta.rs
nodes.summary: Now takes an `Evidence` argument. Statistical evidence short-circuits to (Warning, Advise) before the class/group/context matrix runs, so a guess never blocks a reply.

nodes.label: Skill rule resolution
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/skill.rs
nodes.summary: Passes the finding's evidence into `resolve`, so skill findings obey the same statistical-evidence rule.

nodes.label: Scan rule resolution
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/scan/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Passes the finding's evidence into `resolve` for scan findings.

nodes.label: Unplaceable fixtures
nodes.subtitle: tests/fixtures/writing/unplaceable
nodes.summary: 98 markdown fixtures, each with an `osf-unplaceable` header naming label, kind, target and reason. They cover placeable and unplaceable cases for numbers, phrases, times, names and model-only cases.

nodes.label: Precision/recall measure
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests/unplaceable_measure.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the lint over every fixture, prints a per-kind precision/recall table, and requires 100% precision and recall with no stray findings, excluding the model-only kind.

nodes.label: End-to-end checkpoints
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests/unplaceable_checkpoints.rs
nodes.summary: Drives the compiled binary through the stop hook, the commit-message check and the prompt hook to prove the rule fires, does not refuse on quoted mentions, and that no retired rule id is still advertised.
